items.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the High
Surf Advisory, breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to locally significant beach
erosion is likely. Very localized damage possible to most
vulnerable areas. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of most concern are Avalon, Long
Beach (Peninsula and Belmont Shore). While the surf will
likely be smaller than Marie (from earlier this month), the
lingering erosion effects enhance the vulnerabilities for
locally more significant coastal flooding.

items.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves of 3 to 5
feet. Minor tidal overflows possible, especially Monday and
Tuesday.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas (including Santa Barbara Harbor).
Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant damage
is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Locally moderate coastal flooding impacts
possible but unlikely for areas such as Santa Barbara Harbor.
These impacts may include moderate flooding of sea water over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Additionally, locally moderate
beach erosion is possible.

items.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected due to the combination
of high tides and elevated surf.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 5 AM today.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM today to 5 PM PDT
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding and minor coastal erosion
expected during high tides. Additionally, elevated surf will
lead to strong rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-5 feet expected. Local
sets to 7 feet on south-facing beaches. Morning high tides are
expected to peak between 6.8 and 7.1 feet through Wednesday,
highest on Tuesday morning. These tide predictions have been
corrected to reflect current trends in actual tide
observations.

items.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.87 ft MLLW) at
12:57 PM Monday 9/28, 1.2 ft above normal (7.01 ft MLLW) at
1:30 PM Tuesday 9/29, 1.2 ft above normal (7.03 ft MLLW) at
2:10 PM Wednesday 9/30, and 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW)
at 2:58 PM Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.

items.areaDesc: Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave; Lake Mead - AZ side; Lake Mohave - AZ side; San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley; Southern Clark County; Lake Mead - NV side; Lake Mohave - NV side
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following
areas, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead - AZ side and Lake
Mohave - AZ side, southeast California, including the following
area, San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley, and
southern Nevada, including the following areas, Lake Mead - NV
side, Lake Mohave - NV side and Southern Clark County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms capable of producing flash flooding.
- Locations Affected: Lake Mead, Lake Mohave, Lake Havasu,
Searchlight, Needles, Laughlin, Bullhead City, Meadview, Willow
Beach, Cottonwood Cove.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
